title: Latest Results on Low-Energy Fluctuations in Strange Metals Measured with meV-Resolved EELS
content: The strange metal is a mysterious phase of matter thought to represent a universal limit on the quantum entanglement possible in a many-body system, though this hypothesis remains unproven. In 1989, theorists argued that, if the strange metal is indeed universal, it would exhibit scale-invariant behavior in its dynamic charge susceptibility, χ″(q,ω), at nonzero momentum, q [1].
